# OpenOSINT
> The OSINT toolkit for AI agents: Agent Skill, MCP server and CLI. Passive by default, no API keys needed to start, and every finding cites the tool call that produced it.

## Agent Skill and Claude Code plugin
This repository is a security-hardened fork of OpenOSINT. Run it from a local checkout of this fork: `uvx openosint`, `uvx --from openosint ...`, `pip install openosint`, the `OpenOSINT/OpenOSINT` marketplace and `npx skills add OpenOSINT/OpenOSINT` install the upstream release, which lacks this fork's changes (e.g. `--allow-active-agent`).
Requires [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) and a checkout of this fork whose absolute path is in `OPENOSINT_SRC`. No API keys for the default flow.
- Claude Code plugin (skills; add the MCP server separately): `/plugin marketplace add tusharlab2212/OpenOSINT`, `/plugin install openosint@openosint`, then `/openosint:osint example.com`
- Any Agent Skills client (Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, ...): `npx skills add tusharlab2212/OpenOSINT`, then `/osint example.com`
- Skills: `osint` (passive recon of a domain, IP or organization) and `exposure` (A-F external exposure grade). Passive only; every finding cites its tool call.
- Keyless CLI commands the skills use: `exposure`, `dns`, `rdap`, `whois`, `ip`, `gdelt`, `dorks`.

## Overview
OpenOSINT is a modular OSINT framework that exposes 21 intelligence-gathering tools to large language models via the Model Context Protocol (MCP). It also operates as a standalone CLI, interactive REPL, and browser Web UI for direct human use. No LLM is embedded — OpenOSINT provides the tool surface that an MCP-compatible client (e.g. Claude Code, Claude Desktop) drives autonomously.

## Installation
- This fork, from source: `git clone https://github.com/tusharlab2212/OpenOSINT && cd OpenOSINT && uv run --locked openosint web` (dependencies from `uv.lock`), or `pip install -e .` in the checkout
- Upstream release (not this fork): `pip install openosint`
- Python 3.10+ required

## Claude Code MCP setup
Requires [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/). Passive tools only (20) by default; add `--allow-active --allow-active-agent` for all 25.
`claude mcp add openosint -- uv run --locked --project /absolute/path/to/OpenOSINT openosint-mcp`
With a key: `claude mcp add openosint -e SHODAN_API_KEY=your-key -- uv run --locked --project /absolute/path/to/OpenOSINT openosint-mcp`
Optional, enables active tools (noisy; see README "Passive by default"): append `--allow-active --allow-active-agent`, or set OPENOSINT_ALLOW_ACTIVE=1 and OPENOSINT_ALLOW_ACTIVE_AGENT=1. Both are required: every MCP call is chosen by the client's model.
Claude Desktop / Cursor: `{"mcpServers": {"openosint": {"command": "uv", "args": ["run", "--locked", "--project", "/absolute/path/to/OpenOSINT", "openosint-mcp"], "env": {}}}}`

## Available MCP tools (20)
- `search_email` — enumerate online services registered against an email address (via holehe)
- `search_username` — search a username across 400+ platforms (via sherlock); noisy, off by default (--allow-active)
- `search_breach` — check if an email appears in known data breaches (HaveIBeenPwned v3 API, requires HIBP_API_KEY)
- `search_whois` — retrieve WHOIS registration data for a domain
- `search_ip` — geolocation, ASN, hostname, and org data for an IP address (via ipinfo.io)
- `search_domain` — enumerate subdomains of a target domain (via sublist3r)
- `generate_dorks` — generate 12 targeted Google dork URLs for any target string
- `search_paste` — search Pastebin dumps for mentions of an email or username
- `search_phone` — carrier, country, and line type data for a phone number (via phoneinfoga)
- `search_shodan` — open ports, banners, and CVEs from Shodan (requires SHODAN_API_KEY)
- `search_virustotal` — file/URL/IP verdicts from 70+ antivirus engines (requires VIRUSTOTAL_API_KEY)
- `search_censys` — internet-facing infrastructure and certificate search (requires CENSYS_API_ID + CENSYS_SECRET)
- `search_ip2location` — enhanced IP intelligence: geolocation, ISP, VPN/Proxy/Tor/datacenter flags, sponsored (requires IP2LOCATION_API_KEY)
- `search_abuseipdb` — IP abuse confidence score, reports, country, ISP (requires ABUSEIPDB_API_KEY)
- `search_github` — GitHub profile, repos, commit-discovered emails, username/keyword search
- `search_dns` — A/AAAA/MX/NS/TXT/CNAME/SOA records plus SPF, DMARC, DKIM analysis
- `search_rdap` — domain registrar, registration/expiry dates, name servers and status via RDAP (keyless)
- `search_gdelt_geo` — recent worldwide geolocated news (headline, link, place) from the GDELT 15-minute GKG feed, GeoJSON output
- `search_dorks_live` — live Google search results for dork queries via [Bright Data](https://get.brightdata.com/jx2wfi?sid1=docs&sid2=docs&sid3=search_dorks_live&utm_source=openosint&utm_medium=docs&utm_campaign=docs&utm_content=search_dorks_live) SERP API (referral link: OpenOSINT earns a commission if you sign up through it)
- `scrape_url` — fetch any URL bypassing Cloudflare/CAPTCHA via Bright Data Web Unlocker, returns clean Markdown
- `search_footprint` — entity-type-aware public search-engine footprint (email/username/domain/phone/name), returns structured results + Entity Correlation Graph nodes/edges

## Optional environment variables
- `HIBP_API_KEY` — HaveIBeenPwned API key for breach search
- `IPINFO_TOKEN` — ipinfo.io token for higher rate limits
- `SHODAN_API_KEY`, `VIRUSTOTAL_API_KEY`, `CENSYS_API_ID`, `CENSYS_SECRET`, `IP2LOCATION_API_KEY`, `ABUSEIPDB_API_KEY` — per-tool API keys, see README for full list

## External binary dependencies
holehe, sherlock, sublist3r, phoneinfoga — must be present in PATH

- [Web UI](https://openosint.tech/docs/web-ui/) — local chat, globe and graph
- [Configuration](https://openosint.tech/docs/configuration/) — API keys and environment variables
- [Using OpenOSINT with Bright Data](https://openosint.tech/docs/bright-data/) — setup, cost, example output and errors for `search_dorks_live`, `search_footprint` and `scrape_url`
- [Safety](https://openosint.tech/docs/safety/) — passive mode, tool-call cap, noise labels, responsible use
- [Exposure report](https://openosint.tech/docs/exposure/) — `openosint exposure` external domain grade (beta)
- [Entity graph](https://openosint.tech/docs/entity-graph/) — chat graph view and the optional graph store
- [Troubleshooting](https://openosint.tech/docs/troubleshooting/) — common errors and fixes
- [Tools reference](https://openosint.tech/tools/) — every tool, its noise level and the key it needs

## Hosted version
The engine is open source; a hosted version is built on it:
- [OpenOSINT Cloud](https://app.openosint.tech/?utm_source=llms&utm_medium=llms-txt&utm_campaign=llms) — chat about a domain, an IP address or a company, with a source on every claim. First check free, no account.
